lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Mathematical Habits, Place Value, and Rounding
lessonRef.title: Concept extension: subtraction with regrouping across zeros

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example applies the idea in a new setting. Notice what stayed the same.

items.prompt: You are not sure a word problem is asking you to add or subtract. What should you do first?

steps: Reread the problem and picture what is happening.
Decide whether the total is growing or shrinking.
workedSolution.answer: Reread the problem, picture the situation, and decide whether the amount is growing or shrinking.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Talk through what is different about this case before you start.

items.prompt: A toy store had 540 stickers. They received 167 more stickers. How many stickers are there now?
A toy store had 597 stickers. 475 stickers were given away. How many stickers are left?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: You solved a problem, but the answer seems much too large for the situation. What should you do?
choices: Check the answer against the situation and rework any step that does not make sense.
Skip the problem without trying it.
Multiply every number in the problem together.
Guess an answer and move on to the next problem.

items.prompt: A library had 294 books. They received 153 more books. How many books are there now?
A library had 768 books. 338 books were given away. How many books are left?
You read a word problem and are not sure what it is asking. What should you do first?
choices: Restate the problem in your own words and identify what question is being asked.
Guess an answer and move on to the next problem.
Multiply every number in the problem together.
Skip the problem without trying it.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Explain, in writing, what made this case different from the original one.

items.prompt: A farm had 219 apples. They received 308 more apples. How many apples are there now?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A toy store had 436 stickers. 354 stickers were given away. How many stickers are left?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
